html:
The northernmost people of Eurasia, living on the Taymyr Peninsula of Arctic Siberia. The map shows them there in 1530 and 1600.

They speak a Samoyedic language, like the Enets and Nenets. Unlike the Nenets, they lived mainly by hunting wild reindeer at river crossings during the herds' migrations, along with fishing and fowling, and kept only a few tame reindeer for transport. Russian tax collectors reached them in the 17th century, during the Russian conquest of Siberia. Their shamanic traditions lasted into the 20th century. Fewer than a thousand Nganasan live today.
